summary: Console cost breakdown totals do not match invoice totals (Northbridge Security Labs)
environment: prod (Console + Billing); customer primarily in us-east with some eu-west usage
affected_models: multiple (customer uses mixed chat + embeddings routes; exact models vary by workspace)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports that the Redwood Console "Cost breakdown" totals for Feb do not match their Feb invoice totals. They are treating Console as the authoritative cost number for internal allocation and are seeing a ~6–9% delta depending on workspace.

Customer / account context
- Customer: Northbridge Security Labs (enterprise)
- Deployment: Hosted API + some Dedicated capacity add-on (per CSM notes)
- Stakeholders: Engineering + Finance (invoice reconciliation)
- Customer expectation: Console breakdown totals should reconcile to invoice for the same period when filtered to the same org/workspaces.

Impact
- High trust risk with finance stakeholder; customer is escalating internally.
- Customer blocked on monthly internal chargeback using Console exports.

What customer is seeing
- Console (Cost Breakdown view) totals: lower than invoice.
- Invoice includes line items for: usage (tokens), reserved capacity commit true-up, platform/enterprise fee, and credits/adjustments.
- Customer is currently comparing invoice grand total vs Console usage-only total.

Environment
- Production
- Regions: mostly us-east; some eu-west.

Initial hypotheses (triage)
1) Mismatched reporting window/timezone: invoice is calendar month UTC; Console default filter uses local timezone and/or includes partial current day unless explicitly bounded.
2) Console view currently powered by Standard Cost Model behind flag for some orgs; invoice still sourced from billing ledger logic. If overhead allocation or "non-request-attributable" costs are represented differently, totals will not reconcile.
3) Telemetry lag event around 2026-02-19 triggered drift alert; possible missing late-arriving usage events in Console aggregation, later corrected in invoice.
4) Credits/discounts/commit true-ups appear on invoice but not included in Console breakdown taxonomy (Console currently shows request-attributable runtime costs + configured overhead allocation policy, but not contract artifacts).

Requested outcome
- Provide customer a reconciliation explanation and a concrete, repeatable method to reconcile Console vs invoice.
- If there is an actual defect (e.g., Console includes overhead but invoice excludes, or vice versa), identify and fix.

Support request details / customer message excerpt (paraphrased)
"We exported Console cost breakdown for 2026-02-01..2026-02-29 and the total is $X, but the invoice shows $Y. We need to understand what Console includes/excludes and how to reconcile. Our finance team expects these to match."

Attachments / links (internal)
- Grafana: Cost Model drift dashboard (org-level drift around 2026-02-19)
- Console cost export shared in ticket (uploaded to support case file store; not attached here)
- Slack: #finance thread on overhead allocation policy and reporting windows

Next steps
- Confirm whether customer is opted into Console->Cost Model API integration flag.
- Align on exact date range and timezone used by customer export.
- Compare Console "request-attributable" subtotal to invoice usage subtotal (excluding platform fee, reserved capacity commit true-ups, taxes, and credits).
- Validate whether telemetry lag affected customer’s February window aggregates.

resolution: Resolved with reconciliation guidance and validation. Root cause was expectation mismatch: Console breakdown represents request-attributable usage costs (plus configured overhead allocation) per Standard Cost Model taxonomy, while invoice grand total includes contract-level items (platform fee, reserved capacity commit true-ups, credits/adjustments, taxes). Also identified a Console export labeling issue contributing to confusion. Verified no persistent telemetry undercount for Feb after late-arrival backfill; usage subtotal reconciles within expected tolerance.
workaround: For reconciliation: use UTC calendar month boundaries; compare Console "Usage total" (request-attributable + allocated overhead) to invoice usage subtotal only. Do not compare to invoice grand total. Account for platform fee, commit true-ups, credits/adjustments, and taxes separately.
next_steps: Update Console UI/CSV export labels to clarify what is included/excluded (usage vs invoice).
Add a docs link in Console to Standard Cost Model taxonomy and enterprise invoice reconciliation guidance.
Add monitoring note to Console export flow to avoid materializing aggregates during telemetry lag windows (or display 'data still backfilling' state).
